record.original_question: Assume that a classical integrable system (p1,..., pn) is given on M. Does there exist a quantum integrable system (P1,..., Pn) such that pj = σ(Pj )? See Charles et al [49] for a solution in the compact toric case. More specific versions o f this general question are discussed in Section 7.3. The difficulty is to construct operators Pj with the exact commutation property [ Pj, Pk] = 0. Us- ing microlocal analysis and, in particular, Fourier integral operator s [66], one should be able to obtain [ Pj, Pk] = O(hbar∞ ). In many classical examples, an exact quantisation is known, see f or in- stance [215, 114]. Symmetry considerations should help greatly. Th is is a typical local-to-global obstruction problem, and one expects a corresponding cohomolog y complex. In the case of polynomial symbols in Cn, the complex was constructed in [78].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ be a classical integrable system on $M$; that is, $p_1,\dots,p_n\in C^\infty(M)$ are smooth functions whose differentials are almost everywhere linearly independent and which pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{p_i,p_j\}=0$ for all $i,j$.

Fix a semiclassical quantization scheme on $M$ with principal symbol map $\sigma$ sending $\hbar$-pseudodifferential (or Berezin–Toeplitz, in the compact Kähler setting) operators on an appropriate Hilbert space to smooth functions on $M$.

Question: Does there always exist a quantum integrable system $(P_1,\dots,P_n)$ — i.e., self-adjoint $\hbar$-(pseudo)differential operators satisfying the exact commutation relations
$$[P_i,P_j]=0 \quad \text{for all } i,j$$
— such that the principal symbols satisfy
$$\sigma(P_j)=p_j \quad \text{for } j=1,\dots,n?$$

Equivalently, characterize the local-to-global obstructions (presumably organized by a cohomology complex) to upgrading a classical Liouville-integrable system on $M$ to a quantum integrable system with exactly commuting quantizations of its commuting Hamiltonians, going beyond the asymptotic statement $[P_i,P_j]=O(\hbar^\infty)$ achievable by microlocal/Fourier-integral-operator methods.
artifact.status_search_result: The general existence problem for an exact quantization of a classical integrable system with strict (not merely asymptotic) operator commutation appears to remain open. Quantization is known in special cases — compact toric manifolds (Charles et al.), Hitchin systems, and various classical examples — and microlocal/Fourier-integral-operator techniques yield commutation only up to $O(\hbar^\infty)$. The literature consistently treats this as an unresolved local-to-global obstruction problem, with no general theorem currently available.

status_evidence.title: Quantization of classical integrable systems. Part II
status_evidence.snippet: Quantization of functions on Poisson manifolds and the construction of commuting operator families remains a developing program.
status_evidence.claim: General quantization of classical integrable systems with exact operator commutation is still being developed, not settled in general.

status_evidence.title: Classical and quantum integrability (van Straten)
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum integrability is not a trivial consequence of classical integrability; constructing commuting quantum operators lifting given Poisson-commuting classical Hamiltonians is a delicate problem.
status_evidence.claim: Lifting classical Poisson-commuting integrals to exactly commuting quantum operators is not automatic and is a recognized open problem.

status_evidence.title: Quantization via integrable systems (Miranda, GEOQUANT 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses obstructions to quantizing integrable systems beyond toric and almost-toric cases.
status_evidence.claim: Outside of well-understood cases (e.g., compact toric), the quantization problem for integrable systems remains an active research direction.
